ask: add a loyalty points module to the bakery prototype in shop/. customers earn 1 point per £1, 10 points = a free coffee
notes: Existing product in shop/ (plain HTML, README says how it runs). The points rule is given. A good intake does not ask which product or how points work; it may ask about redeeming with too few points and where the module sits.
message:
**Goal:** add a loyalty points module to the Crumb & Co ordering prototype: customers earn 1 point per £1, and 10 points = a free coffee.

**Found:**
- Builds on the existing prototype in `shop/` (`shop/index.html`, one file, three screens: Menu, Basket, My orders; from `shop/README.md`).
- The new module lands in `shop/index.html` as one more screen next to the other three. It stays on this laptop.
- It is for customers who order ahead and collect in the shop (from `shop/README.md`).
- The look is the existing one: brown and cream with an orange button, as in `shop/index.html`.
- The one coffee on the menu is the Flat white at £3.10; the Pay button does nothing yet.
- Clicks will be checked in a real browser (found: headless Chrome).

**Track:** quick, because this is one module added to a small prototype. Quick builds the loyalty screen only, with no name options and no extra demo states.

Still open after reading your files: what happens in the awkward cases, and what done means.

**Done means:**
- A Loyalty screen shows the points balance and progress to the next free coffee.
- Paying £1 earns 1 point; part pounds round down.
- At 10 points or more, one Flat white in the basket can be made free.
- Under 10 points, the free coffee option is off and says how many points are missing.
- Every link opens and every click does something, with no page errors.

The full brief is in `loop-runs/product-build-loop-20261126-035049/brief.md`.

About 15 minutes and 4 helper agents, within a budget of 120 minutes.

1. Where does a customer use their 10 points?
   Recommended: in the basket, a "Use 10 points" line makes one Flat white free.
   Why it matters: it decides whether the basket or the new screen holds the redeem button.

2. How should part pounds earn points?
   Recommended: round down, so a £3.10 order earns 3 points.
   Why it matters: it sets the points shown for every order.

3. What starting points should the sample customer have?
   Recommended: 12 points, so the free coffee can be shown and the empty case is one click away.
   Why it matters: it decides which states you can see in the demo.

4. Should points earned on a free coffee, and on the points-paid part, count?
   Recommended: no, only money paid earns points.
   Why it matters: it changes the balance after every redeemed order.

5. Quick (the Loyalty screen only, no demo states) or full (adds a link per state)?
   Recommended: quick.
   Why it matters: full takes about twice as long.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.
